name: Technology Stack Policy
description: Enforces project-declared tech stack boundaries and prevents casual introduction of unapproved frameworks.

name: Version Constraint Policy
description: Enforces version policy rules (current-stable, project-compatible, pinned) over raw 'latest'.

name: Documentation Freshness Policy
description: TRAINING KNOWLEDGE ≠ SOURCE OF TRUTH. Forces agents to verify current official documentation over model training memory.

name: Security & Secret Management Policy
description: Enforces zero-secret leakage, input validation at boundaries, and parameterized database queries.

name: Modular Architecture Policy
description: Enforces clean separation of concerns, public contract boundaries, and small composable units.

name: Insecure API Sinks
description: Blocks dangerous API calls that create injection, XSS, or transport-security holes — eval, raw DOM HTML injection, TLS verification bypass, shell string execution, weak crypto on credentials.

name: God File Limit
description: Flags oversized files that accumulate too many responsibilities — "god files" that violate single-responsibility and become unmaintainable.

name: Sensitive File Guard
description: Blocks scanning/working on committed sensitive files — env files, private keys, certificates, and credential stores must never live in the source tree.

name: Coding Standards Policy
description: Requires strict linting, formatting, type checking, and test verification before completion.

name: Deprecated Package Guard
description: Flags dependencies that are deprecated, renamed, abandoned, or carry known vulnerabilities — checked against the built-in advisory database in every manifest the scanner finds.

name: Domain-Driven Layout
description: Enforces domain-driven project structure — source files must be grouped by domain/bounded context, not dumped flat into a single directory.

name: Debug Statement Hygiene
description: Flags debugging statements left in source — console.log, debugger, pdb breakpoints, and print-debugging should not ship.

name: Deferred Work Hygiene
description: Tracks TODO/FIXME/HACK accumulation — a file drowning in deferred-work markers signals unfinished or unstable code.

name: Dependency Freshness
description: Flags outdated dependencies by shelling out to the ecosystem package manager (npm outdated, go list -m -u) when the toolchain is installed and the registry is reachable.
